Issue: The monthly series is explicitly marked SAMPLE DATA, NOT FOR POSTING. Publishing it still suggests a measured growth path.
Recommended fix: Remove the series. Show only the supplied, team-reported 350K snapshot until the history is verified.

Issue: The heading groups transparent addresses, historical Connect wallets, encrypted accounts, indexed profiles and monthly app users. The row visually invites an invalid ranking.
Recommended fix: Rename it Reported adoption and keep the scope and timeframe inside each cell. Label Aztec as historical.

Issue: The 95%+ matching result reads as a general measure of live wallet exposure. The removed notes contained the testnet limitation.
Recommended fix: State controlled-test scope beside the chart, including that the Bitcoin and Solana tests used testnets.

Issue: Every new operator becomes a buyer is unconditional, while the deposit rate is zero. The essential condition appears below the headline.
Recommended fix: Put the condition in the title: priced deposits would create demand for SN25.

Issue: The title says the base and bull cases imply returns, but no model linking the operating assumptions to those valuations is supplied. The illustrative qualification disappeared with the captions.
Recommended fix: Label the ranges as illustrative assumptions, keep them distinct from model-derived forecasts, and state the observed variable.

Issue: Four long evidence paragraphs compete with takeaway text and oversized metrics. The small reading text weakens the hierarchy.
Recommended fix: Cut the evidence copy to the minimum required and set it on the same 17px body scale.

Issue: A topic label interrupts the action-title storyline. Its section links also retain old page numbers after the deck was shortened.
Recommended fix: Use a sentence describing the section takeaway and update the links to the retained slide order.

Issue: Component labels and category explanations are materially smaller than the surrounding narrative. The chart requires close reading at presentation size.
Recommended fix: Raise the chart labels to the shared readable scale and retain component amounts beside the bars.

Issue: Event descriptions, years and the two timeline tiers use several small text sizes. The detail loses legibility before the main timeline does.
Recommended fix: Use a consistent label scale and keep the two tiers explicitly distinguished by scope and date.

Issue: The use-case table uses 13px body text and numerous tiny outlined logo pills. At the PDF size, the body is below the requested 12pt floor.
Recommended fix: Increase the evidence text to 17px, simplify the logo treatment and use compact role labels.

Issue: The title runs to roughly four lines and dominates the narrow column. The chart loses the benefit of a short takeaway.
Recommended fix: Shorten it to Privacy demand alone does not set token value, keeping two lines.

Issue: Coverage universe is a topic label, and the right-hand page references still use the old numbering.
Recommended fix: State the value-capture distinction in a sentence and renumber the section navigation.

Issue: Five project columns carry long paragraphs at 14.8px. Bigger fonts alone would overflow the fixed slide.
Recommended fix: Edit the copy before increasing type, retain the column orientation, and give the rows explicit heights.

Issue: Direct capture, governance and conditional deposits all appear as solid black badges, although they describe different economic states.
Recommended fix: Use filled badges for direct mechanisms and outlined badges for indirect or conditional mechanisms, with explicit text.

Issue: The left title wraps to about five lines. Relative wording such as current use is not tied clearly to the frozen data.
Recommended fix: Use Zcash prices in future private use and name the snapshot period in the slide metadata.

Issue: The logarithmic comparison mixes FDV, market cap, staking and user funds. With the caption removed, the axis type and USD basis are easy to miss.
Recommended fix: State logarithmic USD scale in the main chart context, and keep each metric named.

Issue: The small labels below the bars contrast with a very large historical peak. Today is stale once the slide circulates.
Recommended fix: Raise the labels and replace Today with the date of the price snapshot.

Issue: The title is unnecessarily long, while the small per-year unit and effective dates carry essential meaning.
Recommended fix: Shorten the takeaway and make annual issuance and effective dates equally legible.

Issue: The section title is long and descriptive, rather than stating the central uncertainty. The link numbers retain the original deck positions.
Recommended fix: State that UR has users while operator demand has yet to begin, and update navigation numbers.

Issue: The title occupies roughly five lines before the supporting text begins. The narrow column becomes top-heavy.
Recommended fix: Use UR reports 350K monthly users and reserve the body for the deposit condition and measurement scope.

Issue: Small node text and removed explanatory captions make it difficult to distinguish live routing and scoring from the conditional deposit link.
Recommended fix: Increase diagram labels and explicitly say the dashed deposit link is inactive at a zero rate.

Issue: The headline multiples can be read as upside targets. The removed caption carried the market-cap and illustrative qualification.
Recommended fix: Keep market-cap comparison in the headline context and state that the chart is not a valuation model.

Issue: The quadrant and ranked pathway table use small text and small status chips. Live and speculative pathways need stronger separation.
Recommended fix: Use the shared body scale and retain explicit Live, Zero at launch and Speculative labels.

Issue: Live VPN usage, research programmes and third-party business metrics share a dense table. Research does not look sufficiently different from current activity.
Recommended fix: Keep the roadmap status explicit and make clear that peer metrics illustrate scale, not forecast UR revenue.

Issue: Bull and base show capital multiples, while bear shows percentage loss under one heading. Readers have to convert between units.
Recommended fix: Use market-cap multiples throughout: 12×–30×, 1.8×–3.6× and 0.24×–0.60×.

Issue: The title calls all seven rows dated events, although four are launch triggers or recurring indicators. The rows are not in chronological order.
Recommended fix: Rename the scope and group scheduled milestones before launch and recurring triggers.

Issue: The current web export hides slide numbers, while divider lists retain old page numbers. Project logos also vary between footers.
Recommended fix: Restore continuous 1–23 numbering, use one Khala footer position and retain project logos within the evidence area.

Issue: Removing all visible source captions also removed dates and material chart qualifications. A frozen price cannot remain labelled Today.
Recommended fix: Keep the date and material measurement limitations visible. Keep detailed source references in a separate evidence register.

Issue: The rotated Same conclusion text is small and decorative. It adds another reading direction between already parallel profiles.
Recommended fix: Remove it and retain the grid gutter.

Issue: The peer column mixes ARR and valuation. Although the cell text names them, the header does not explain the distinction.
Recommended fix: Label the column Market reference and metric, retaining ARR versus valuation in each cell.

Issue: Instrument Serif, Host Grotesk and JetBrains Mono create a third typographic voice for small labels.
Recommended fix: Use Instrument Serif and Host Grotesk in the slides, with a small consistent scale.

Issue: x multiples, lowercase web2, all-caps pills, gradients and animation rules add avoidable variation.
Recommended fix: Use × consistently, standardise Web2, replace unnecessary pills with plain labels, and remove motion and gradients.
